prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Denver for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
"Best" depends on your specific needs (single tooth vs full-arch, bone grafting required, sedation, budget, timeline). Rather than one name, here’s how to find the best Denver clinician for your dental implant — and what to expect and ask at a consult.

Who usually places implants
- Oral and maxillofacial surgeons (OMS) — surgical specialists for complex cases, extractions, bone grafting, sedation/general anesthesia.  
- Periodontists — specialists in gums and bone; commonly place implants and manage bone regeneration.  
- Prosthodontists — specialists in restoring teeth and making the implant crown, bridge, or denture look/function best.  
- General dentists with advanced implant training — often do straightforward implants and coordinate with specialists for complex work.

Credentials and experience to look for
- Board certification or specialty training (DDS/DMD + residency in OMS, periodontics, or prosthodontics).  
- Memberships/fellowships in professional organizations (AAOMS, AAP, ACP, ICOI) and continuing education in implants.  
- Years/number of implants placed and success rates (ask directly).  
- Experience with the type of case you have (single implant vs full-arch, immediate loading, bone grafts, sinus lifts).  
- Use of CBCT 3D imaging and digital planning/guided surgery; use of reputable implant systems (Straumann, Nobel/ NobelActive, ZimmerBiomet, etc.).  
- Good before/after photos and patient references or reviews.

Questions to ask at a consultation
- Are you a specialist (periodontist, oral surgeon, prosthodontist) or a general dentist?  
- How many implants have you placed, and what is your success rate?  
- Do you perform CBCT imaging and 3D surgical planning?  
- Which implant systems do you use and why?  
- Will you do the restoration (crown/denture) or refer to a prosthodontist?  
- Do I need bone grafting or sinus lift? If so, what are the costs and timeline?  
- What anesthesia/sedation options are available?  
- What is the projected timeline from implant placement to final restoration?  
- What are all costs, including surgical fees, implant parts, abutment, crown/denture, and follow-up?  
- Do you offer any warranty/guarantee for failures or complications?  
- Can I speak with previous patients or see photos of similar cases?

Where to find and compare Denver providers
- Ask your general dentist for a referral.  
- Check Colorado Dental Association or Denver Metro dental society directories.  
- Use review sites (Google, Healthgrades, Yelp) and read long-form reviews and before/after galleries.  
- Look at clinicians’ websites for bios, training, CBCT imaging, and case photos.  
- Get at least two consultations and compare treatment plans, timelines, and total costs.

If you want, I can
- Help narrow options if you share your ZIP code and whether you need a single implant, multiple implants, or a full-arch solution.  
- Provide a list of questions to take to consultations or a template to compare two or three quotes.

Which would you prefer — tips only, or help finding specific providers near you?
